case.question: Shortlist three Abu Dhabi areas for our takeaway-led pizza and kebab branch.
expected: Three Abu Dhabi-specific candidate areas with support

answer.headline: Three Abu Dhabi shortlist areas for a takeaway-led pizza and kebab branch: Al Zahiyah, Khalidiya (Al Khubeirah), and Al Manhal/Al Wahda — each validated by an observed competitor footprint and site checks before commitment.

sections.title: Shortlist: three candidate areas and why

items.text: Al Zahiyah: Papa Johns lists a pizza branch by the Abu Dhabi Mall parking entrance there, and the Abu Dhabi tourism authority describes Al Zahiyah as an established district with long-running restaurants and parks, near the Corniche, Al Maryah Island, and Abu Dhabi Mall. For a takeaway window, this is a fit hypothesis only — tourism descriptions are not unit availability or demand evidence, so confirm an actual retail unit, loading access, and short-radius delivery reach.

Khalidiya / Al Khubeirah: Papa Johns lists its ADNOC 913 Khalidiya branch on Ash Shoulah Street, Al Khubeirah, Al Khalidiyah; tourism describes Khalidiyah Mall nearby with cafes, restaurants, a food court, cinema, and bowling. Mall-adjacent trade means we would be competing for the same pizza occasion as an incumbent — differentiate on Jordanian kebab sandwiches and mixed meat-topped pizza rather than head-on price.

Al Manhal / Al Wahda: Papa Johns lists an Al Wahda Mall branch on Hthaymah Street in Al Manhal, and tourism describes Al Wahda Mall with a Lulu Hypermarket and multiple dining options. Suits a compact takeaway unit serving surrounding streets; the mall-anchored competitor means the site check must establish whether a non-mall unit can be reached and supplied easily.

Khalifa City surfaced in evidence as a listed area (Allo Beirut lists a Sector 32 branch with advertised 8 AM–12:30 AM hours; Operation Falafel is listed in Madinat Khalifa A on Talabat), but none of our curated records describe a takeaway-format unit or its access there. Treat it as a fourth, exploratory candidate rather than joining the three-area shortlist.

sections.title: What to verify at each shortlisted site before choosing

items.text: Every area above rests on directory and tourism descriptions, not verified rents, footfall, customer mix, or shop availability. Measure the properties yourself: count passing pedestrians and vehicles across weekday lunch, weekday dinner, and Friday evening; log parked-vehicle turnover; and list competing pizza, kebab, and shawarma outlets within your intended delivery radius.

Run the same test on all three: confirm the unit is licensed for food preparation, has adequate grease/extraction and gas provision, and allows a pickup counter plus a delivery staging spot without blocking the pavement.
Compare quoted rents and any service-charge or fit-out obligations across the three on a like-for-like basis (size, frontage, visibility, parking) before shortlisting to two.

assumptions: Branch format is takeaway-led (user profile), so seating-led mall locations were assessed for their surrounding catchment rather than as mall units.
Startup budget and monthly rent budget are unset in the profile, so no rent band or site size is proposed here.
The concept is Jordanian meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches (user profile), treated as the differentiator versus listed pizza and Lebanese-sandwich operators.

Run three-shift traffic and competitor counts within a defined delivery radius for each area, and record the results in a comparable table.

**Shortlist: three candidate areas and why**

- **Fact:** Al Zahiyah: Papa Johns lists a pizza branch by the Abu Dhabi Mall parking entrance there, and the Abu Dhabi tourism authority describes Al Zahiyah as an established district with long-running restaurants and parks, near the Corniche, Al Maryah Island, and Abu Dhabi Mall. For a takeaway window, this is a fit hypothesis only — tourism descriptions are not unit availability or demand evidence, so confirm an actual retail unit, loading access, and short-radius delivery reach. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>) [2](<https://visitabudhabi.ae/en/where-to-go/marinas-waterfronts/al-zahiyah>)
- **Fact:** Khalidiya / Al Khubeirah: Papa Johns lists its ADNOC 913 Khalidiya branch on Ash Shoulah Street, Al Khubeirah, Al Khalidiyah; tourism describes Khalidiyah Mall nearby with cafes, restaurants, a food court, cinema, and bowling. Mall-adjacent trade means we would be competing for the same pizza occasion as an incumbent — differentiate on Jordanian kebab sandwiches and mixed meat-topped pizza rather than head-on price. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>) [3](<https://visitabudhabi.ae/en/things-to-do/shopping/Khalidiyah-Mall>)
- **Fact:** Al Manhal / Al Wahda: Papa Johns lists an Al Wahda Mall branch on Hthaymah Street in Al Manhal, and tourism describes Al Wahda Mall with a Lulu Hypermarket and multiple dining options. Suits a compact takeaway unit serving surrounding streets; the mall-anchored competitor means the site check must establish whether a non-mall unit can be reached and supplied easily. [1](<https://www.papajohns.ae/stores>) [4](<https://visitabudhabi.ae/en/things-to-do/shopping/al-wahda-mall>)
- **Inference:** Khalifa City surfaced in evidence as a listed area \(Allo Beirut lists a Sector 32 branch with advertised 8 AM–12:30 AM hours; Operation Falafel is listed in Madinat Khalifa A on Talabat\), but none of our curated records describe a takeaway-format unit or its access there. Treat it as a fourth, exploratory candidate rather than joining the three-area shortlist. [5](<https://www.allobeirutstreetfood.com/locations>) [6](<https://www.talabat.com/uae/restaurant/704423/operation-falafel-khalifa-city--ad-7?aid=1483>)

**What to verify at each shortlisted site before choosing**

- **Proposal:** Every area above rests on directory and tourism descriptions, not verified rents, footfall, customer mix, or shop availability. Measure the properties yourself: count passing pedestrians and vehicles across weekday lunch, weekday dinner, and Friday evening; log parked-vehicle turnover; and list competing pizza, kebab, and shawarma outlets within your intended delivery radius. [2](<https://visitabudhabi.ae/en/where-to-go/marinas-waterfronts/al-zahiyah>) [3](<https://visitabudhabi.ae/en/things-to-do/shopping/Khalidiyah-Mall>) [4](<https://visitabudhabi.ae/en/things-to-do/shopping/al-wahda-mall>)
- **Proposal:** Run the same test on all three: confirm the unit is licensed for food preparation, has adequate grease/extraction and gas provision, and allows a pickup counter plus a delivery staging spot without blocking the pavement.
- **Proposal:** Compare quoted rents and any service-charge or fit-out obligations across the three on a like-for-like basis \(size, frontage, visibility, parking\) before shortlisting to two.

**Assumptions and limitations**

- Branch format is takeaway-led \(user profile\), so seating-led mall locations were assessed for their surrounding catchment rather than as mall units.
- Startup budget and monthly rent budget are unset in the profile, so no rent band or site size is proposed here.
- The concept is Jordanian meaty pizza and kebab sandwiches \(user profile\), treated as the differentiator versus listed pizza and Lebanese-sandwich operators.
